Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
2.2 Part of speech tagging experiments We perform POS experiments using Universal De- pendencies (UD) (Nivre et al., 2016) data for 41 languages.3 We use the evaluation sets from Ze- man et al. Table 2 shows M-BERT zero- shot results for four European languages. We see that M-BERT generalizes well across languages, achieving over 80% accuracy for all pairs.

Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
M-BERT’s performance, on the other hand, is ﬂat for a wide range of overlaps, and even for language pairs with almost no lexical overlap, scores vary between 40% and 70%, showing that M-BERT’s pretraining on multiple languages has enabled a representational capacity deeper than simple vocabulary memorization.5 To further verify that EN-BERT’s inability to generalize is due to its lack of a multilingual rep- resentation and not an inability of its English- speciﬁc word piece vocabulary to represent data in other languages, we evaluate on non-cross-lingual NER and see that it performs comparably to a pre- vious state of the art model (see Table 3).

[3] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 Introduction
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
Dan Garrette In this paper, we empirically investigate the degree to which these representations generalize across languages. We explore this question us- ing Multilingual BERT (henceforth, M-BERT), re- leased by Devlin et al.

[4] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 Introduction
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?

[5] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
(2019) arXiv:1906.01502v1 [cs.CL] 4 Jun 2019 as a single language model pre-trained from monolingual corpora in 104 languages, is surprisingly good at zero-shot cross-lingual model transfer, in which task-speciﬁc annota- tions in one language are used to ﬁne-tune the model for evaluation in another language.

[6] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 Introduction
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
(2019) as a single language model pre-trained on the concatenation of mono- lingual Wikipedia corpora from 104 languages.1 M-BERT is particularly well suited to this probing study because it enables a very straightforward ap- proach to zero-shot cross-lingual model transfer: we ﬁne-tune the model using task-speciﬁc super- vised training data from one language, and evalu- ate that task in a different language, thus allowing us to observe the ways in which the model gener- alizes information across languages.

[7] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
To understand why, we present a large number of probing experiments, showing that transfer is possible even to languages in different scripts, that transfer works best between typologically similar languages, that monolingual corpora can train models for code-switching, and that the model can ﬁnd translation pairs.

[8] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 Introduction
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?

[9] Source: 1906.01502.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 Introduction
Title: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
